To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the focal adhesion protein LPXN interacts with the actin binding protein CaD and modulates CaD phosphorylation via recruitment of the MAPK ERK.
the focal adhesion protein LPXN interacts with and phosphorylates the actin-binding CaD to regulate cell migration and invasion of human prostate cancer cells.
the actin-binding focal adhesion protein LPXN interacts with the actin binding protein CaD and modulates its phosphorylation status via ERK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new targets for PCa therapy.
the role of the actin binding protein caldesmon in prostate cancer cell adhesion and migration.
the identification of novel mechanisms that contribute to the migration and invasion of metastatic PCa cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LPXN is a key regulator of cytoskeletal dynamics in PCa cells.
LPXN is a key player in PCa cell migration, and that LPXN-mediated CaD phosphorylation is a potential therapeutic target in advanced PCa.
LPXN regulates the phosphorylation status and thus the activity of CaD by recruiting the ERK kinase to the actin cytoskeleton.

the interaction of LPXN with CaD is essential for PCa migration, which is facilitated by ERK-dependent phosphorylation of CaM.
